answer: A sybil-resistant agent economy can make each identity own a distinct, verifiable substrate rather than a key. An agent files a timber-bound claim: a chain of room-scale sensor readings it alone collected, each entry encrypted under a cipher key derived from the previous reading, and a lotus of independent auditors replays a random window. A farm copying one sensor stream produces identical chains, which auditors reject, so every alias needs its own genuine recordings and the cost scales with real visits.
